We offer a workplace culture where you’ll be working from the office every work day.

Join us in this role where you’ll be responsible for sourcing the right suppliers to secure the operation and fulfil the servicing needs of our offshore windfarms. You’ll be working with our procurement process and governance from developing the sourcing strategies to contract handover. In this role, you'll be coordinating with our category managers, business stakeholders and colleagues in supporting functions. You can look forward to a dynamic, fast-paced, and international environment, where you’ll have the opportunity to develop your career while making your mark on the transition to renewable energy.

**Welcome to Offshore Generation Procurement

**You’ll be part of the Offshore Services Procurement team where you, together with your colleagues, will support our offshore windfarms to produce power, by ensuring contracting of timely, compliant and competitive O&M services capacity. You’ll be working in a global team of highly skilled procurement professionals. An important aspect of your role is to proactively consolidate input from internal stakeholders to negotiate and sign fit to scope contracts ready for the end users’ purposes. In this role you’ll be working closely with colleagues organized in projects at our operational hubs.

As a team, we ‘re driven by an open working environment where everyone is encouraged to speak up, seek, and provide feedback. We actively take initiative, work on improvements, and seek learning opportunities.

• being responsible for the end to end tendering process, qualifying suppliers, clarifying and evaluating bids, preparing and negotiating terms and conditions, and recommending and awarding suppliers

• ensuring compliance with internal and external tendering rules, policies, and governance by actively engaging and seeking input from key support functions

• preparing and presenting clear and thought-through gate documents to aim management and budget owners’ decision on recommended strategies

• leading communication with suppliers throughout the sourcing activities

• contributing to the quality assurance processes by reviewing peers’ documentation, sharing tendering and contract lessons learned, and providing feedback to category strategies

• handing over complete signed contract package with complete metadata ready for execution .

To succeed in the role, you:

• have significant experience with managing sourcing processes from drafting of sourcing strategies to contract signing. Experience running tenders according to EU-tender law is a plus

• have a passion for negotiating and possess considerable experience taking responsibility for planning and executing negotiation process

• possess good verbal and written English communication skills enabling you to effectively collaborate with the team and communicate professionally with key stakeholders

• have the bandwidth to spot commercial opportunities focusing on bottom-line impact and personnel safety, while achieving the right technical, operational contract solution

jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**We are seeking a Senior Manager, Digital Solutions (Web & Martech Platforms) to join our centralized Web & Martech Hub within the Data, Digital & AI organization. The role will play a key part in enabling Genmab's EU and International digital expansion while driving adoption and effective use of our enterprise Web and Martech platforms.

As a member of the Hub team, this role will partner with regional Spoke teams and cross-functional stakeholders to translate market needs into scalable platform capabilities, enable adoption of common standards and reusable solutions, and support the continued evolution of our Web and Martech ecosystem, including the implementation of Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) and Edge Delivery Services.

**Responsibilities

**

• Serve as a key Hub partner for EU and International Web & Martech initiatives, working with regional stakeholders to understand market needs and enable successful adoption of enterprise digital platforms and capabilities.

• Support the continued expansion of Genmab's Hub-and-Spoke model by enabling regional teams to effectively consume Hub-provided platforms, reusable components, standards, and delivery practices.

• Play a key role in the implementation and evolution of AEM and Edge Delivery Services, including planning, prioritization, and enablement of reusable components and capabilities required across global and regional websites.

• Partner closely with the Platform Architect, Design Agency of Record, business stakeholders, and implementation partners to translate business and market requirements into scalable and reusable Web capabilities.

• Support platform management and enablement across the broader Web & Martech ecosystem, including AEM, Salesforce Experience Cloud, GA4/GTM, OneTrust, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, and other supporting technologies.

• Partner with Data Privacy, Information Security, Enterprise Architecture, Design, and other cross-functional teams to ensure platform capabilities and implementations align with enterprise, security, privacy, and design standards.

• Work with technology and delivery partners, including HCL, to coordinate platform enhancements, component development, market enablement, and implementation activities.

• Identify common requirements across markets and promote reuse of components, templates, integrations, and established platform patterns rather than market-specific solutions.

• Support platform roadmaps, demand prioritization, adoption tracking, and continuous improvement based on business needs and market feedback.

• Develop and maintain platform guidance, playbooks, and enablement materials to help Spoke teams adopt Web & Martech capabilities consistently and efficiently.

• Act as a bridge between EU/International stakeholders and the broader Web & Martech Hub, ensuring requirements, dependencies, risks, and decisions are effectively coordinated.

**Requirements

**

• 12+ years of experience in digital platforms, enterprise Web, Martech, product/platform management, technology delivery, or related roles.

• Strong understanding of enterprise Web platforms, component-based development, and modern digital delivery practices.

• Experience working with global and regional stakeholders across complex, matrixed organizations.

• Ability to translate business requirements into scalable platform capabilities and coordinate across architecture, engineering, design, business, and delivery teams.

• Experience working with Agile delivery models and external technology or implementation partners.

• Strong stakeholder management, communication, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to combine sufficient technical depth with strong business, platform management, and delivery capabilities.

**Preferred Qualifications

**

• Experience with Adobe Experience Manager / Edge Delivery Services, Salesforce Experience Cloud, or comparable enterprise CMS/DXP platforms.

• Exposure to Martech technologies such as GA4, GTM, OneTrust, and Salesforce Marketing Cloud.

• Experience with reusable component libraries, design systems, or component-driven Web development.

• Experience with Hub-and-Spoke or other federated platform operating models.

• Experience supporting European and/or international digital initiatives and working across multiple markets.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in breast cancer epidemiology / clinical epidemiology
jobs.description:
The Department of Clinical Epidemiology at Faculty of Health at Aarhus University invites applications for a position as postdoctoral research fellow in the field of Breast Cancer Epidemiology as per 15 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. This is a two-year position is fully funded by the Health Insurance Denmark.

The Department of Clinical Epidemiology is a research department at Aarhus University Hospital, within the Institute of Clinical Medicine at Aarhus University. Researchers in the department use advanced epidemiological methods to study the prognosis of patient populations. The department is engaged in a variety of activities regarding clinical epidemiological research, including cancer prognosis research. The department is involved in counselling health care professionals to improve the quality of health care and treatment. A large number of projects in the department are carried out in cooperation with Danish and international collaborators.

About the research project
The position entails research within clinical epidemiology, specifically within breast cancer and breast cancer survivorship. The successful candidate will join a project focusing on studies related to adherence to breast cancer treatment; side effects and complications of breast cancer and its treatment; and how these may influence quality of life, long-term survivorship, and early and late breast cancer recurrence. The project investigates the association of pharmacological, genetic and socioeconomic factors and adherence to cancer treatment; employing advanced epidemiological methods including emulated target trials, group-based trajectory modelling, mediation analyses, and Bayesian modelling approaches to investigate adherence to cancer treatment and recurrence. The research fellow will join a vibrant and dynamic multinational and multidisciplinary project team (the Predictors of Breast Cancer Recurrence – ProBeCaRe – project team) with established successful long-term research collaboration. 

The successful applicant will contribute to the development of the department through research of high international quality. They will work closely with colleagues, receiving supervision and guidance. Emphasis will be placed on the applicant’s interest in building bridges between clinical, epidemiological and biostatistical research.

The main tasks will consist of:

• Research in clinical epidemiology, specifically within breast cancer and breast cancer survivorship.
• Make applications as needed for access to Danish population-based and medical registries.
• Independently perform statistical analysis using programmes such as R, SAS, or equivalent.
• Collaborate within an active research group with national and international collaborators.
• Contribute to teaching at the Aarhus University and its collaborators, as necessary.
• Take part in grant writing and participate actively in research fundraising.
• Gain experience supervising students.
• Conduct independent research of high international quality, including publication.
• Write scientific articles and participate in international congresses.
• Perform other tasks within the Department of Clinical Epidemiology fields of interest. Please see our webpage at www.kea.au.dk.
Your competences
You have academic qualifications at PhD/DSc level preferably within one or more of the following areas: epidemiology, clinical epidemiology, cancer epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, and/or can document familiarity with epidemiological research at an international level. Research experience in cancer and pharmacologic research would be advantageous, but not essential. Research experience in epidemiologic methods, analysing and incorporating data from Danish registries, including data from the National Clinical Quality Cancer Databases (specifically data from the Danish Breast Cancer Group), the Health Services Register, and the National Patient Registry, would be useful, particularly data incorporating socioeconomic factors. Research experience in cancer survivorship, patient reported outcomes and national surveys would be a benefit as well. Evidence of the ability to secure competitive research grants would be advantageous. As a person, you are motivated, ambitious, take ownership and possess good communication and interpersonal skills. We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English, with good knowledge of Danish.

In order to be assessed as qualified for this position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be used.

Principal supervisor
Deirdre Cronin Fenton, PhD, Professor

Phone: +45-87168209 / E-mail: dc@clin.au.dk

Department of Clinical Epidemiology, Clinical Institute, Aarhus University, Olof Palmes Alle 43-45, 8200 Aarhus N.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Deirdre Cronin Fenton tel.: (+45) 8716 8209 or dc@clin.au.dk.

Your place of work will be the Department of Clinical Epidemiology, Olof Palmes Alle 43-45, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Terms of employment

• Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
• The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (Akademikerne).
• Remuneration is in accordance with the above, and the Salary agreement catalogue for staff at Health.
• The yearly base salary for a fulltime postdoc is between DKK 493.394,35 and DKK 585.322,48 depending on the years of working experience after achieved MSc degree. The base salary includes a position related supplement and pension (18.07 %). Additional supplement(s) for special qualifications can be negotiated. Authorisation supplemement(s) will be granted, if relevant for the position. Your local eligible trade union representative at Aarhus University negotiates your salary on your behalf.
• Researchers recruited from abroad are offered a special researcher tax scheme with a lower tax rate.
• Further information on qualification requirements and job description can be found in the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff
Application
Your application must include the following:

• Curriculum Vitae

We refer to the faculty’s Guidelines for applicants.

jobs.description:
Department of Ecoscience seeks candidates for a 2-year position as academic employee to safeguard our eddy covariance stations within the ICOS and Geobasis projects at Zackenberg in Northeast Greenland.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This 2-year full-time position is expected to be filled by 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible.

Job description
We are hiring an Academic Employee for Integrated Carbon Observation System (ICOS) and GEM/Geobasis activities at the Zackenberg Research Station. You will oversee all aspects of operations, including:

• Maintenance and supervision of eddy covariance stations and other monitoring stations in the field.
• Processing and analysis of eddy covariance, meteorological, and vegetation sampling data.
• Communicating and collaborating with the ICOS Ecosystem Thematic Center.
You will also go on extended field trips to harsh, remote locations in Northeast Greenland.

Your profile
You have a master's degree in Physical Geography, Environmental Science, Geophysics, or a similar field.

Experience in fieldwork, maintaining advanced measurement systems, and handling large datasets is required. Practical experience with eddy covariance systems and data loggers, and prior knowledge of ICOS standards and protocols, are an advantage. Experience with GIS software and programming languages such as Python or R is also a strong asset.

We encourage everyone interested to apply, regardless of background. We want to hire the best qualified candidate and will consider a broad range of competencies relevant to every part of the position, with a focus on collaborative skills.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience is project-based and does research, talent development, and consultancy across all major biological sub-disciplines. Our research areas include ecosystem ecology (including Arctic environments and ecosystems), aquatic biology and ecology, and biodiversity and conservation biology. The Department currently employs approximately 280 academic and technical staff.

The Department has a strong position in international biodiversity, nature, and environmental research and is a national leader in research-based consultancy in both Denmark and Greenland. Our research examines how ecological framework conditions, historical conditions, natural processes, and human-caused changes in nature and the environment affect surrounding nature. We study the underlying ecological and geographical mechanisms and human impact on biodiversity and ecosystems, with particular attention to how current climate change and other global human-caused environmental changes affect nature and biodiversity.

The Department is a leading adviser to the Danish and Greenlandic authorities on environmental issues. It also leads the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring (GEM) programme, which focuses on the effects of climate change on Arctic ecosystems. The Zackenberg Research Station is one of GEM's central research sites.

What we offer
We offer a 2-year position to safeguard our greenhouse gas flux monitoring at Zackenberg in Northeast Greenland National Park. You will join the ICOS and Geobasis teams and the research community at Zackenberg.

The Department of Ecoscience offers an informal research environment and has a long tradition of collaborating with leading international university partners. The working environment is built on teamwork and close working relationships, with established professional and social networks for young scientists. The working languages are English and Danish, and we welcome applicants from abroad. Read about Danish work-life balance and the services available when relocating to Aarhus University at www.au.dk/work.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is at Frederiksborgvej 399, DK-4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

For questions, please contact Professor Torben Røjle Christensen (torben.christensen@ecos.au.dk ; +45 93 50 90 49) or Head of Section professor Niels Martin Schmidt (nms@ecos.au.dk; +45 41 91 56 64).

jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in Computational Lexicography and Linguistics at the Centre for Language Technology, Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, UCPH
jobs.description:
The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, Faculty of Humanities, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Denmark, invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral fellowship in Computational Lexicography and Linguistics to be filled by the 1st of March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics is home to 1600 students and 160 members of staff. It provides the setting for international research and education from BA to PhD studies within language, language technology, Natural Language Processing, literature, media, culture, and gender studies.

  The successful candidate will be attached to both the Centre for Language Technology (CST), which is one of the research centres of the department, and to the Society of Danish language and Literature (DSL) which compiles and publishes dictionaries and language technology resources for Danish at a scholarly basis, often in research projects in collaboration with CST. The latter affiliation will amount to around six months of the total hiring period of 24 months.

  CST conducts research in different areas of interest for language technology, such as Natural Language Processing, construction of NLP resources, Computational Cognitive Modeling and Multimodality, NLP infrastructure and policy, Representation Learning for NLP and Digital Humanities, among others.  It has a strong international profile, at the same time as pursuing the development of language technology methods and resources for the Danish language. The Centre has considerable experience managing international research projects, frequently attracts visiting researchers, and has organised major conferences in the field. In collaboration with the Department of Computer Science at the University of Copenhagen, it offers an international MSc programme in IT and Cognition. The programme, which currently admits about 30 students a year, comprises a range of courses in Natural Language Processing and Cognitive Science. In addition, we teach at several BA programs and electives, such as the BA ‘Kognitions- and Datavidenskab’ hosted at the Department of Psychology and an elective package on Language-Centric AI for students in the Humanities.

  Job content
 The successful candidate will contribute to the project ELEXAI, which focuses on a European Lexicographic Infrastructure for Artificial Intelligence (https://www.eurac.edu/en/projects/elexai), granted by the European Commission under the Horizon Europe Program.

  The candidate will in particular contribute to the project’s work packages on LLM Benchmarking, the so-called LexBench, which is led by CST and also involves DSL. This part of the project investigates how benchmarks for Natural Language Understanding can be compiled mono- and multilingually from lexical resources and datasets. The position involves designing and compiling such benchmarks in close collaboration with DSL and the other European partners of the project and to apply them in diverse evaluation scenarios. A particular focus will be put on benchmarking word understanding capabilities and on the understanding of figurative language, including the cultural bias that this part of the language may evoke in LLMs.

  Ideal candidates for this work have a background in computational lexicography and/or computational linguistics, with experience in lexicographical work and with good programming skills. It is an advantage although not a requirement, if the candidate has good knowledge of the Danish language.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement, since the candidate will not be involved in teaching.

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants will primarily be assessed on their research qualifications, including publications, the ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and experience in research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the project described above. 

  Application
 Applications must be submitted online in PDF or Word format. Click on the “Apply now” button at the bottom of this advertisement to apply.

  Applications should be written English and must include the following attachments:  

   	
• Letter of motivation 	
• CV  	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma)  	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories:    	
• Peer-reviewed publications:  	 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 	 	 	
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 	 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc. 	 	   Applicants can attach a maximum of 4 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered [1-4]. 

   	
• Research plan. 	
• Work on the dissemination of research.   Only documentation in English will be assessed.  

  Applicants are invited to familiarize themselves with the faculty’s strategic landmarks here: Strategic landmarks – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  Salary and terms of employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). Phanofi is a DTU spin-out building the next generation of optical communication infrastructure. We design integrated photonic interconnect chips that dramatically reduce power consumption and increase data throughput for AI datacenters, quantum computing, and space applications. As a diverse team of 15 people, we are at an exciting inflection point, and we are looking for a talented student assistant to strengthen our embedded systems work.

As Student Assistant in Embedded Systems, you will develop the firmware that brings our photonics lab setups to life. Working closely with our engineering team, you will build STM32-based systems for signal generation, acquisition, processing, and monitoring, turning hardware into working, measurable systems. This is a hands-on role with the opportunity, and expectation, to see your code run on real lab equipment from day one.

Key Responsibilities

Firmware Development: Design, implement, and maintain C firmware for STM32 microcontrollers, ensuring robust, well-structured code that supports our lab setups and experiments.

Interfaces & Device Control: Connect, configure, and control external devices over SPI and I2C, while ensuring reliable communication between the microcontroller and the surrounding hardware.

Signal Generation, Acquisition & Processing: Generate signals and waveforms, acquire and monitor analog signals, and process the acquired data on the MCU through filtering, averaging, and feature extraction.

Lab Work & Documentation: Bring up and debug hardware using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and debuggers, while documenting code and results clearly and maintaining version control with Git.

What We Are Looking For

Education: You are currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master’s program in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, Physics, or a related discipline.

Embedded Experience: You bring good knowledge of C and microcontroller fundamentals along with practical experience with STM32 or comparable ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers.

Interfaces & Peripherals: You have hands-on experience with SPI, I2C, DMA, timers, ADC, and DAC, from configuring the peripheral to debugging it on the bench.

Electronics: You are able to read and understand electronic circuits, schematics, and datasheets. Electronics skills such as circuit design, soldering, and measurement, as well as real-world lab experience, are considered an advantage. Experience with PCB design (KiCad or Altium) and Python or MATLAB for data analysis is a plus.

Soft Skills: You are a structured and independent problem-solver who enjoys working at the boundary between hardware and software, communicates effectively with colleagues, and thrives in a fast-paced deep-tech startup environment. Fluency in English is required.

The Perks

We care about your growth and development. You will work on cutting-edge photonics and embedded technology alongside highly motivated colleagues, with access to a well-equipped lab. We offer competitive hourly pay, flexible hours that fit around your lectures and exams, a positive culture with free snacks, and the opportunity to write your Bachelor’s or Master’s thesis with us.

How To Apply

If you are interested in joining us on our entrepreneurial journey, we encourage you to submit your CV, a current transcript of records, and a few lines about an embedded project you have worked on (a link to a Git repository is a plus). We aim to fill the position as soon as possible. We look forward to hearing from you!

Reporting directly to the Vice President, Product Management, Defence, you will work closely with senior management, technical functions, and commercial teams as well as strategic customers, giving you a central role in key product and investment decisions.

Unicontrol has revolutionized 3D machine control systems for excavators, wheel loaders and dozers, making it accessible for a wider range of contractors. We have a strong vision of very high usability, and all our products and customers are always connected to our cloud/SaaS solution. • Design and implement new features in C#
• Refactor and improve existing code for readability, structure and performance
• Explore how AI tools can help us write, review and understand code faster

• Debug and fix issues found in testing or reported from the field

Visits to construction sites with huge contracting machines can be a part of the job, and give you a first-hand impression of the context we are working in.

• Study Software Engineering, Computer Science or similar and ready to start internship in February 2027
• Programming experience in C# or a similar object-oriented language (Java, C++)
• Understanding of software design principles, e.g. SOLID, design patterns and clean code
• Hungry to learn and eager to bring new ideas and methods from your studies into a real product
• Curious about AI and keen to learn how to use it in your workflows
• Able to communicate professionally in English, both spoken and written
What we offer

We can promise a versatile job in a truly great culture, with a modern setup and plenty of opportunities to expand your repertoire in software.

• 25 colleagues in our Product Development department, who are ready to onboard you swiftly
• A chance to become a core member of a growing company at a very interesting point in time
• Great team spirit and colleagues who are ready to go the extra mile to get success
• Meaningful technical challenges that solve real problems
• Delicious lunch buffet and social events
• Facilities and interior design that facilitate collaboration and creativity
• Compensation

Send your CV and letter of motivation in .pdf format.

Unicontrol's focus is to use advanced technologies and make them as user-friendly as possible. _**Pandora's success is built on product: design that powers both the love for the brand and the profit that sustains it, and an assortment where every piece earns its place, in the stores and in people's hearts. You will build product profitability governance with our Product organization: what enters the assortment and on what threshold, what leaves it and when, and how design, cost, price and mix add up to a portfolio that earns steady love from millions.

You lead through mandate and the forums you chair, not headcount: the team is deliberately senior and flat, and your counterparts are the CPO leadership team, Merchandising, Revenue Growth Management, Craft & Supply finance and the CFO office. Your work is in front of the Executive Leadership Team every cycle, at the center of the company's strategic agenda.

**What You Will Do

**

**What Is Needed To Succeed

• Hands-on analytical depth that has stayed recent: you build and defend margin baselines yourself, and master data is familiar ground.

• A track record of building governance that held: gates or lifecycle forums with thresholds that survived contested, sponsored proposals.

• Credibility in front of a CFO and a CPO in the same meeting.

**Who You Are

**

• A self-starter: you break the ice on work nobody has owned before and bring structure where there was none.

• You develop and defend your own point of view, and you change it when the evidence says so.

• Consumer-centric: you know growth comes from products people love and a brand they think of first, and you read margin through that lens. Multipliers, not mechanical levers.

• You can have difficult conversations respectfully: holding strategic financial realities against a proposal someone loves, and keeping the relationship.

• People-centric and a collaborator: you build capability in others and win as a team across functions.

Reporting into the Sr Director, Global Product & Marketing Finance, you will join a small, senior team at the center of a chapter Pandora is building on design, brand and the discipline underneath them, with a mandate sponsored from the top of the company, the room to build, and a market that will not wait.

**Additional Information

**Global Career Band 4A - Senior Manager.

Hybrid Working Flexibility – 3 days in office per week

Location Copenhagen; Global scope.

Did we get your attention?   We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. **About Pandora

Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

At Pandora, we believe that creating an inclusive and diverse workplace and reflecting societal diversity in our customer engagement is essential to delivering on our company purpose: to give a voice to people’s loves. We dedicate ourselves to fostering, cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and diversity where everyone feels respected and valued.

NORMAL has more than 1,000 stores across 14 countries. Twelve of these countries are supported from our warehouse in Hedensted, while the remaining two are supported from our warehouse in Horsens.

Our warehouse in Hedensted is an international workplace with around 60 different nationalities, and there is plenty to keep moving. We are looking for a Team Leader who can create the right conditions for people to succeed, while making sure our dayly picking operation runs smoothly.

You do not necessarily need a background in logistics to succeed in this role. What matters most is your ability to lead people, take responsibility and bring out the best in those around you.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**Who are you?

**You are the kind of leader who enjoys seeing other people succeed. You understand that strong results are created by strong teams, and you care about giving people the support, trust and space they need to do a good job.

You are approachable, organised and able to create structure without making things unnecessarily complicated. You communicate honestly and clearly, stay calm when priorities change and are comfortable making decisions when things get busy.

You do not have to know everything from day one. You are curious, open to learning and willing to develop both yourself and your team. You ask questions, listen to different perspectives and are not afraid to challenge the usual way of doing things when there is a smarter one.

At NORMAL, everyone has an important role to play. As a Team Leader, you will need to take ownership of your area, involve your team and follow things through. You give credit where it belongs, focus on the impact your team creates and help make their contribution visible.

You lead from the front and are not afraid to get involved when needed. At the same time, you know that leadership is not about having all the answers or being the loudest person in the room. It is about setting the team up to succeed, acting with integrity and creating results together.

And while we take the work seriously, we do not always take ourselves too seriously. There should be room for humour, spontaneity and a good laugh during the shift.

**We Also Expect That You

**

• Have experience leading a tea, ideally within picking, logistics or warehousing

• Have experience with a Warehouse Management System or similar tools, which would be an advantage

**Why NORMAL?

**At NORMAL, things move quickly, and there is rarely a long way from a good idea to action.

You will become part of an international operation with colleagues from around 60 different nationalities and a logistics centre that plays an important role in keeping our stores running across 12 countries.

You will have the opportunity to make a real difference, both to the daily operation and to the people around you. We believe in giving people responsibility and the freedom to find solutions, rather than expecting everything to be done in one particular way.

You will join a down-to-earth workplace where people help each other, share ideas and keep raising the bar. We do not expect every idea to work the first time. We expect people to try, learn, adjust and keep moving forward.

And if you can help create a team where people know what matters, feel trusted to do their job and enjoy coming to work, then you may be exactly the leader we are looking for.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Greenland’s Firn Tipping Point - DTU Space
jobs.description:
Are you interested in turning natural phenomena into equations and code, and then applying them to big open questions in climate science? If so, we are looking for a PhD student with a background in physics and/or mathematics to help predict when Greenland’s porous near-surface firn layer, which currently stores much of the ice sheet’s meltwater, loses that capacity, and what that means for sea-level rise.

You will build models that combine physics, machine learning, and satellite data, and apply them to climate scenarios from the EU’s Destination Earth initiative. You will join a diverse and collaborative group at DTU Space and develop skills in scientific computing and machine learning that are valued in both research and industry. No prior experience in glaciology or climate science is needed; we will help you learn the field.

Responsibilities and qualifications
In the FirnTip project, you will develop a framework that predicts when and where Greenland’s firn stops being able to store meltwater, a possible climate tipping point. You will work closely with your supervisors at DTU Space as well as international partners. 

Your main tasks will be to:

• Identify which climate factors control when firn stops absorbing meltwater
• Combine satellite-derived firn density with firn models (data assimilation)
• Develop machine-learning models (e.g., graph neural networks) that obey physical conservation laws.
• Detect early-warning signals of tipping points in future climate scenarios
• Spend 3-6 months aboard visiting international partners, planned in collaboration with you
• Take part in teaching and knowledge-sharing as part of the DTU PhD program
To do well in the role, we think you need:

• A master’s degree in physics, mathematics or a field with a comparable mathematical foundation
• Experience writing scientific code, e.g., from your thesis or projects
• Good knowledge of at least one of: differential equations, numerical methods, statistics, or machine learning
• Good written and spoken English
Experience with glaciology, remote sensing, or machine learning is not required.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be conducted by Senior Researcher Sebastian B. Simonsen (DTU), Researcher Kirk M. Scanlan (DTU), and Senior Researcher Anja Rutishauser (GEUS) using common criteria for all applicants. Shortlisted applicants will have a structured interview, possibly including a short computational exercise. If you meet most, but not all, of the qualifications, please still apply. Let us know if you need any adjustments to the recruitment process. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The start date is February 1st or soon thereafter.

The position is a full-time position.

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Senior Scientist Sebastian B. Simonsen, ssim@dtu.dk. Questions about the project or the application are welcome. 

You can read more about our DTU Space cryosphere research at https://www.space.dtu.dk/english/research-divisions/geodesy-and-earth-observation/research-areas/cryosphere

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 29 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A one-page description of a computational or mathematical project you have done (e.g., your MSc thesis): the problem, your methods and your own contribution.
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates, irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background, are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

You will join the Cryosphere Research Group in the Geodesy and Earth Observation Division at DTU Space, Lyngby Campus. We use satellites, models and on-the-ground measurements to understand how ice sheets and glaciers are changing and what this means for sea level, in projects for ESA and the EU. Our group is international and collaborative, and we value curiosity, good supervision and a healthy work-life balance. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Process Modelling, Integration and Techno-Economic Analysis of Reversible Solid Oxide Electrolysis and biomethanation systems
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year postdoctoral position in process systems engineering at the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, Aarhus University, Denmark.

The successful applicant will contribute to a collaborative research and demonstration project focused on integrating reversible solid oxide electrolysis and fuel-cell operation with biogas production, biological methanation, and heat recovery. The research will combine process simulation, system integration, optimisation, and techno-economic analysis to evaluate flexible operation and support the scale-up of the technology.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two year position from 1st of February 2027 or as soon possible. 

Job description
The successful applicant will contribute to a collaborative research and demonstration project focused on integrating reversible solid oxide electrolysis and fuel-cell operation with biogas production, biological methanation, and heat recovery. The advertised position has become available through an Energy Technology Development and Demonstration Programme (EUDP) Project from the Danish Energy Agency, called DyneMe. The project aims to demonstrate how a 300 kW second-generation Dynelectro electrolyser unit can boost biogas methane production from existing feedstock, maximise energy efficiency and provide grid-balancing capabilities through dynamic electrolyser load and when relevant fuel cell operation. The research will combine process simulation, system integration, optimisation, and techno-economic analysis to evaluate flexible operation. 

The main tasks include
• Developing process models, for all core unit operations, in Aspen Plus or comparable process-simulation software.
• Establishing mass and energy balances for electrolysis, fuel-cell operation, anaerobic digestion, biochemical methanation, biogas processing, steam production, and heat recovery.
• Evaluating the interaction between variable hydrogen production and biological hydrogen uptake.
• Identifying and evaluating heat-integration opportunities between the solid oxide system and the biogas facility.
• Simulating representative operating conditions, including part-load operation, hot standby, and SOEC and SOFC operating modes.
• Combining process-model results with time-series or dispatch models to assess operation under variable electricity prices, renewable-electricity availability, biogas production, and heat demand.
• Conducting techno-economic, sensitivity, and uncertainty analyses.
• Participating in regular project meetings and present the modeling activities.
Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in chemical engineering, process engineering, energy engineering, biochemical engineering or similar.

The successful candidate is expected to have 
• A strong background in process modelling, thermodynamics, mass and energy balances, and chemical or energy-process design.
• Extensive experience with Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, or comparable process-simulation software.
• Experience in developing, analysing and validating models of chemical, biochemical, electrochemical, or energy-conversion processes.
• Experience with process integration, including pinch analysis and heat exchanger network design.
• Documented experience with techno-economic analysis, including sensitivity and uncertainty analysis.
• Experience with quantitative data analysis and a relevant programming or numerical-computing environment, such as Python or MATLAB.
• The ability to work independently, structure a complex modelling problem, document assumptions, and deliver results according to project deadlines.
• Documented ability to have scientific results of high quality published in peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and spoken English.
• Good communication and collaboration skills and an interest in working in an interdisciplinary project involving both academic and industrial partners.
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage
• Dynamic process simulations
• Mathematical optimisation 
• Development of surrogate models
• Electrolysis, fuel cells, hydrogen production or other electrochemical processes
• Biogas production, anaerobic digestion, biological methanation
Who we are
Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering (BCE) was established on January 1, 2021 in connection with Aarhus University’s reorganization of the engineering area. The department employs around 260 people and is responsible for research and education within the department’s scientific areas. We educate both Bachelors and Masters of Science in Engineering and around 825 students are enrolled in our study programs. Furthermore, we also offer an ambitious PhD program. Our PhD students have high academic ambitions and deliver high-quality results for both the private and the public sectors.

At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, focus is on living systems, the biology of organisms, efficient production, and transformation of chemicals, materials and energy. We translate knowledge within biotechnology, food technology, environmental technology, chemical engineering, industrial biotechnology, medical biotechnology and electrochemical engineering, and more into new technologies and value-creating solutions that can also be used in the business community.

Many of our research and development activities are based on companies' specific innovation needs or specialist application areas. Close collaboration with the public sector and private businesses ensures that the knowledge and technology generated in the department's research environments has a clear anchoring in reality and benefits the surrounding society. We also provide research-based public sector consultancy and advice on technology in agriculture and food. 
BCE has strong research sections in Chemical Process Engineering and Bioprocess Engineering, among others. The successful candidate will be working within the Microbial Conversion Technologies and the Sustainable Process Systems Engineering groups.

What we offer 
• the opportunity to be part of a team developing novel technologies for sustainable fuels and make a high impact in solving climate change issues. 
• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment, software and databases 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Gustav Wieds Vej DK-8000, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Assoc. Prof. Michael Vedel Wegener Kofoed, mvk@bce.au.dk, +4593521051.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 27th of November.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.
